book.title: The Lucky Ones: A Memoir
book.summary: A moving memoir by a survivor of anti-Muslim violence in contemporary India that delicately weaves political and family histories in a tribute to her country’s unique Islamic heritage—“a must-read in our warring world today” (NPR) “A harrowing survivor’s tale, an important history lesson, and a desperate warning from someone who has seen the tragic effects of ethnic violence.”—Time A KIRKUS REVIEWS BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR • FINALIST FOR THE PEN/GALBRAITH AWARD FOR NONFICTION In 2002, Zara Chowdhary is sixteen years old and living with her family in Ahmedabad, one of India’s fastest-growing cities, when a gruesome train fire claims the lives of sixty Hindu right-wing volunteers and upends the life of five million Muslims.

evidence: trade publisher signal: Crown / Penguin Random House

argument.statement: Anti-Muslim ethnic violence in contemporary India devastates survivors and families while threatening the country’s distinctive Islamic heritage.

book.rationale: The book primarily recounts the author's personal experiences as a survivor of anti-Muslim violence, making it a memoir, while also addressing significant political and ethnic themes related to contemporary India.
